source.title: Attention SAEs Scale to GPT-2 Small
source.authors: Connor Kissane; robertzk; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: Uses SAE features, direct feature attribution, and an induction-behavior heuristic to investigate induction behavior in GPT-2 Small, rather than the original training-time measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports induction-feature behavior in GPT-2 Small, but does not measure training dynamics, in-context-learning loss by token position, or a loss-curve bump. SAE reconstruction and interpretability metrics do not bear on the claim. The 50% attribution cutoff is used to select features, not reported as an independent result.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE-method post. It takes GPT-2 Small's already-known induction heads (L5H5, L6H9) as ground truth to check that its attention-SAE features and heuristics recover them. The 117/158 count measures how well the method's heuristic performs, not whether induction heads exist or how they work. GPT-2 Small is not an attention-only model, so V1 is out of scope. There is no training-dynamics or in-context-learning loss measurement, and no comparison across models, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the paraphrase overweights induction. The authors conclude that attention SAEs scale to GPT-2 Small and recover interpretable features in every layer, including the known induction, local-context and high-level-context families plus new ones. They take the 117/158 Layer 6 result as showing that their induction-detection technique generalizes to GPT-2 Small.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes SAE features with direct feature attribution and a heuristic induction-behavior test; it does not reproduce the original training-time analysis of induction-head formation and in-context-learning dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer and feature-selection criteria differ across the reported analyses; the Layer 6 behavior result uses features selected by attribution to L6H9.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention-layer SAE features in GPT-2 Small middle-to-late layers behave as 'X is next by induction'. Feature attribution shows they are computed from the token after the earlier matching token, and they are mostly attributed to known induction heads (L5H5, L6H9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-head computation decomposes into sparse token-specific 'X is next by induction' features in attention-output SAEs of pretrained models.

record.problems: The authors describe the feature investigations as shallow and say they did not systematically check all features. The reported Layer 6 behavior count depends on heuristic selection and a stated pass-rate threshold; the number of randomly selected negative-control features is not given. The Layer 5 example is qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant induction result omitted. Training-SAE reconstruction metrics and feature-family findings unrelated to induction are excluded.

untested.parts: All of it: formation by composition with a previous-token head, in small attention-only models.
All of it: no training dynamics are measured.
All of it: no in-context-learning loss by token index.
There is no new evidence across families, sizes or runs. Induction heads in GPT-2 Small are taken as already known.

record.verdict_notes: A figure of GPT-2 Small induction head scores, computed from attention on random repeated tokens, is shown but given no numbers; it is used as a reference, not as a result. The reader's labels (V1 and V4 supports) are dropped: GPT-2 Small is outside V1's scope, and the induction results here validate the method rather than test induction heads.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test formation by composition with an earlier previous-token head in small attention-only transformers. It examines features in GPT-2 Small and their attribution to known induction heads.
Tests GPT-2 Small only; does not compare model families, sizes, training runs, other architectures, or modalities.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Used direct feature attribution to inspect an induction feature and its source positions; reported its effect on logits.
rows.measure: Induction-pattern source attribution and logit effect
rows.value: The feature is described as moving the previous instance of X following the first <token> to compute the feature, and as boosting the logits of X (the example is the ‘-’ feature).
rows.note: Qualitative example; no numerical effect size is given.
rows.check: This is a qualitative feature-level example in GPT-2 Small, which is not a small attention-only model. It does not test the formation or composition mechanism in V1. Induction behaviour in GPT-2 Small was already known, so the example does not test V4. Record it under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied the induction-behavior heuristic to features selected by attribution to the L6H9 induction head.

conditions.value: at least 50% weight-based attribution to L6H9

rows.measure: Number of features meeting the induction-behavior criterion
rows.value: 117 of 158 possible induction features passed the heuristic.
rows.note: The reported count is for the selected Layer 6 features, not a model-wide prevalence estimate.
rows.check: This is the method's own performance: features are first selected by attribution to the known head L6H9 and then filtered by the heuristic. It is a validation of the selection method, not a result on induction heads.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Measured decoder-weight attribution of an induction feature to attention heads.
rows.value: The decoder weights mostly attribute the feature to a subset of GPT-2 Small induction heads; L5H5 is identified for this example.
rows.note: Qualitative attribution; no proportion is reported.
rows.check: This is decoder-weight attribution to a known induction head, used to validate the SAE. No proportion is reported, and it bears on no version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Applied the induction-behavior heuristic to randomly chosen features with low attribution to L6H9.
rows.value: None of the selected features passed the induction-behavior heuristic.
rows.note: The text does not state the number of randomly selected control features.
rows.check: This is a negative sanity check on the method's heuristic, not a result on the claim. The number of control features is not given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 Small induction-feature examples and Layer 6 heuristic analysis
reader_labels.reason: The reported feature behavior follows the repeated-token induction pattern and is attributed to known induction heads (r1-r3). The study does not establish the proposed composition mechanism.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Induction-behavior features are reported in this model, including 117 Layer 6 features meeting the stated heuristic (r1-r3).
